answer: Each epoch, every seat in a randomly drawn grove is hit at the same unannounced instant with a memory-hard task and a tight deadline. While it runs, a nebula of scattered, unrelated verifier nodes sends echo pings to each seat; matching round-trip delays and stalls reveal seats sharing one host, and those seats collapse into one paid slot. Since the whole grove is tested at once, a farm cannot time-share a box across its fakes: each extra identity needs its own dedicated machine awake and distinct at that moment, again every epoch.
